paper.title: Combinatorial Gaussian Process Bandits with Probabilistically Triggered Arms

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB-PTA with GP-sampled expected base arm outcomes
unmapped: Each of the m base arms has a known context vector x_i in [0,1]^d; the expected outcome function f with f(x_i)=mu_i is a sample from a GP with known kernel (posterior variance bounded by 1)
Learner has access to an exact computation oracle OPT returning an optimal super arm for any given base-arm mean vector (knows problem structure, e.g. triggering structure)
Reward function is monotone in mean vector (Assumption 2) and Lipschitz (Assumption 3) or TPM-Lipschitz (Assumption 4)
settings.definition_quote: The learner selects a super arm S(t) from a subset of 2^[m], denoted by I. The arms in S(t) may trigger other arms via a stochastic triggering process ... The learner observes the individual outcomes of each base arm in S'(t), and a reward that depends on S'(t) (semi-bandit feedback). ... Y_i(t) := mu_i + eps_{i,t}, where eps_{i,t} are i.i.d. zero mean Gaussian random variables with known variance sigma^2 ... We assume that there exists a function f : X -> R, sampled from a GP, such that f(x_i) = mu_i.
